goal: how do i add an image?
preamble: Adding an image looks like one action, but Docs is really asking you two questions: what kind of thing are you adding, and where is it coming from. The second one matters more than it seems — some sources put a copy of the picture inside the document, and some only leave a pointer to a file that lives somewhere else. You're about to walk through both questions in order.
generalization: Anything that isn't text you typed gets added from the Insert menu — images, tables, drawings, page numbers, all of it. And whenever Docs offers you a list of sources, it's asking whether the document should own a copy or borrow from elsewhere. Uploading means the picture travels with the document; a URL or a linked account means the document depends on something outside itself still being there.

steps.intent: Nothing in the document needs changing — you're putting something in it that isn't there yet. Docs keeps that distinction strictly: menus for altering what exists, and one menu for adding what doesn't.
hints: You're not formatting or editing anything. You're bringing in something new.
The menu bar at the top, between View and Format.

wrongHints.Format: Format works on things that already exist in the document — it can resize and align your image later, but it can't bring one in.
wrongHints.Edit: Edit handles actions on existing content: undo, copy, paste, find. Pasting an image can work, but it skips the choice of source that we want you to see.

steps.intent: This menu is a list of every kind of thing that can go into a document — a table, a chart, a footnote, a page break. Pick the one that says what you're adding, and the little arrow will tell you Docs isn't done asking questions yet.
hints: Everything in this menu is a type of object. You want the one for pictures.
Near the top of the Insert menu, above Table.

wrongHints.Drawing: Drawing opens a blank canvas for you to make something from shapes and lines. That's for creating an image, not for bringing one in.
wrongHints.Chart: A chart is a picture too, but Docs builds it from numbers you supply. You already have the image.

steps.intent: Your turn. This last list is the 'where from' question — each option is a different place a picture might live, and each one carries a different consequence for the document. Choose the one that takes a file off your own machine and puts a copy inside the document, so it stays there no matter what happens to the original.
hints: Some of these options leave the picture where it is and point at it. One of them brings it in for good.
The first entry in the submenu that just opened.

wrongHints.By URL: A URL is a reasonable guess — it's fast and needs no file. But the document only remembers the address. If that page moves or goes offline, the image goes with it.
wrongHints.Drive: Drive is close, and it does keep the file safe. It's still a separate file though, with its own sharing settings — someone who can open the document may not be able to see the image.
wrongHints.Photos: Same idea as Drive: the picture stays in your account and the document reaches out for it. Uploading takes a copy instead.
